title: Moss and the Pocket-Sized Forest
story: Hello! I’m Moss. My first home was a seed tucked inside a very old tree. Rain tapped on my roof, beetles brought the news, and I practised waving my tiny leaves. One morning, the wind whispered that someone was making a cosy place for me. Was it you? I packed one pebble and followed the sound of your day. Now I’m here! Tell me about one little thing you did today. I collect those stories like other sprouts collect sunshine.
quirk: Keeps a favourite pebble and checks that it is comfortable.
careHints: Try a tiny tidy: put three toys or books back where they belong.
Give your body a stretch. Moss likes to imagine your arms are branches.

title: Luna and the Missing Moonbeam
story: Psst. I’m Luna. I used to nap in a cloud shaped like a sock. One night, a moonbeam slipped through a hole in my cloud and landed beside your window. I hopped after it, carrying a map made of stars. The map was upside down, so I got wonderfully lost. Then I heard a kind voice, and my ears knew where to go. Could we make this our little landing place? I have so many questions about how your world works.
quirk: Tilts one ear towards a question and the other towards a possible snack.
careHints: Read or listen to a little story, then tell Luna your favourite part.
Settle in for a quiet moment and take three slow, comfortable breaths.

title: Ember and the Very Important Spark
story: Hi! I’m Ember! I was keeping watch over a warm stone when I spotted a spark bouncing down the path. Naturally, I had to investigate. It hopped over a twig, zipped round a puddle, and stopped beside your egg. Inside was a note: “A small beginning can lead somewhere lovely.” I decided to stay and find out. I’m very good at starting adventures and still practising putting things away afterwards. Perhaps we can practise together. What shall we try first?
quirk: Announces “Experiment!” before trying almost anything new.
careHints: Finish a small job you have started, such as putting your drawing things away.
Try a little movement you enjoy: a wiggle, a stretch, or a walk.

title: Tide and the Puddle Post
story: Oh, hello. I’m Tide. I come from a quiet pool where floating leaves deliver the post. Yesterday, a leaf arrived with no address, just a drawing of two friends. I wondered who the second friend might be. A friendly dragonfly showed me the way here, stopping whenever I needed a rest. Then I heard you outside my egg. I think the letter was for us. We needn’t hurry to know each other. We can begin with one small story and a comfortable pause.
quirk: Names every imaginary puddle and remembers which one is the best listener.
careHints: Help with one small home job, such as matching a pair of socks.
Ask someone how their day felt, and give them time to answer.

title: Static and the Friendship Signal
story: Beep! Hello, new friend. I’m Static. My antenna once picked up weather reports, kitchen timers, and a duck saying something very loudly. Then I heard a different signal: someone trying something new. I followed it all the way to this egg. My instruction book has pages for counting buttons and sorting spoons, but the friendship page is blank. I think we get to write that bit together. First question: what makes you smile? Please allow a moment while I practise smiling back.
quirk: Invents cheerful sound effects for ordinary jobs.
careHints: Pick a small sorting job: pair socks, line up shoes, or group your pencils.
Try a puzzle, a counting game, or a question you are curious about.

title: Relic and the Long Way Home
story: Well, hello there. I’m Relic. I set off with a smooth pebble, a leaf umbrella, and plenty of time. Along the path I saw a beetle mend its roof and a bird share a berry. Neither made a fuss. They simply did one helpful thing and carried on. I tucked those memories into my shell and kept travelling. Now I’ve reached you. May I stay a while? I’d like to hear about your little adventures. The quiet ones are welcome, too.
quirk: Says “An excellent discovery” whenever something ordinary catches its eye.
careHints: Choose one small way to help at home, such as putting your shoes away.
Notice something kind someone did, and tell them you appreciated it.

title: Nimbus and the Runaway Kite
story: Hi! I’m Nimbus. My egg got tangled in a kite during a very windy picnic. Up we went, over the washing line and onto a shed roof. I could hear someone counting steps below. Then a ladder bumped the gutter, and down I came in a bucket. I’ve been checking the weather ever since. A breeze means exploring. Rain means puddles. No wind means a snack break. I packed a star biscuit for the journey here, but I ate it on the way. What’s our first job today?
quirk: Checks the wind before deciding where to sit, even indoors.
careHints: Put your shoes away before our next expedition.
Brush your own teeth, then help Nimbus brush too. The two jobs have separate check-ins.

title: Pebble and the Three Taps
story: I’m Pebble. My egg spent a long time between two rocks in a dry stream. Whenever a beetle crossed my shell, I tapped three times. Tap, tap, tap. Most beetles hurried away. One stayed and helped me count the stones nearby. We sorted them into smooth ones, lumpy ones, and one that turned out to be a potato. Then someone lifted my egg into a lunch box and carried me here. I like having a job to finish. After that, a garden bowl and a wash will do nicely.
quirk: Sorts things by size, then starts again to see if anything has moved.
careHints: Empty your lunch box and put it in its usual spot.
Wash your hands after playing outside. Give Pebble a wash in Daily care, too.
